question.worked_solution:
Since we have an overall common factor of $5$, we start by dividing our equation through by $5.$ This gives 

$$
6{n}^{3}+3{n}^{2}-4n-2=0.
$$

Next, we factor by grouping. Notice that when grouping the smaller terms, we factor out the negative sign.

$$
\begin{aligned}6{n}^{3}+3{n}^{2}-4n-2 & = \\ (6{n}^{3}+3{n}^{2})-(4n+2) & = \\ 3{n}^{2}(2n+1)-2(2n+1) & = \\ (2n+1)\cdot 3{n}^{2}-(2n+1)\cdot 2 & = \\ (2n+1)(3{n}^{2}-2) & .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we set each factor equal to $0$ and solve:

- Setting the factor $(2n+1)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2n+1 & =0 \\ n & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Setting the factor $(3{n}^{2}-2)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{n}^{2}-2 & =0 \\ 3{n}^{2} & =2 \\ n & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the solutions to the given equation are $-\frac{1}{2}$ and $\pm \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}.$
